resolved_findings.resolution: The positive sesquilinear form is made Hermitian by direct polarization, then Schwarz is proved with the second-linear convention. For r>||b||, the norm-convergent binomial series inside the abstract C*-algebra gives r^2*1-b*b=(rs)*(rs). The norm bound and GNS representation no longer depend circularly on a concrete functional calculus. The null-space, completion, bounded action and cyclic unitary equivalence arguments were checked.
The I_A/D example now assumes a complete basis and D=dim(H_A)>=2; a proper span K gives P_K/D. Partial-trace coefficients agree with the stated inner-product convention.

The blank binary tape, n nonhalting states plus one halting state, only left/right moves, and final-transition step count are explicit. The effective finite-control simulation supplies a computable state count. The proof does not transfer the numerical BB(6) value between machine models.
Abstract purity is separated from the rank-one characterization for the full matrix algebra M_N(C). The diagonal-subalgebra warning prevents the former overgeneralization.

The general-surface smooth Green remainder is now proved locally, not inferred from a sphere-only reference. The combined four-dimensional Laplacian gives a smooth right-hand side, and the local Weyl-lemma argument proves joint smoothness. The 1/(2*pi) fundamental solution, spectral summability and the GFF covariance factor 2*pi were checked. The final three changed auxiliary files were reread before their hashes were refreshed.
The independent full-matrix characterization is now its own atom. The approximate-Haag note locally reintroduces its algebra, pure state and GNS data instead of relying on its parent outline.

resolved_findings.title: Fusion-category axioms omit additivity and tensor bilinearity
resolved_findings.original_finding: Every existing object being a finite sum of simples does not assert that arbitrary finite sums or a zero object exist. The stated meaning of complex linearity constrains composition but not the tensor bifunctor.
resolved_findings.resolution: The definition now explicitly requires all finite biproducts including zero, finite-dimensional morphism spaces, finite simple classes, decomposition into simples, and a tensor bifunctor complex-linear in both morphism variables. The C*-norm, adjoint, rigid and unitary monoidal requirements are explicit. The former one-object counterexample is excluded. EGNO Definition 4.1.1 and Remarks 4.2.2 and 9.4.7 were checked; 4.2.2 is a Remark, correcting the review's former label 'Example'.

sources.locator: Definition 4.1.1, printed p.65 (PDF page 82); Remark 4.2.2 illustrates why tensor bilinearity is separate.

resolved_findings.title: Four-leg tensor model and claimed Gram-test graphs disagree
resolved_findings.original_finding: 4I0Q quantifies over finite connected graphs while using exactly the four-leg tensor defined in 4I0O. Accounting for all tensor legs gives 4n=2m+b. The packet's (n,m,b)=(3,2,2) and (4,4,2) examples do not satisfy that condition.
resolved_findings.resolution: Both atoms now use finite connected square-lattice vertex regions, four legs per vertex, all unused legs as boundary, and 4n=2m+b. The path3 and square4 examples have b=8 and rank D^7; their Gram factors remain 1 and D. The packet withdraws the former b=2 evidence and records physical Z2 contractions. The reviewer independently executed the unchanged parent test block over all 256 boundary columns and all 65536 Gram entries in each example, obtaining the expected factors 1 and 2. Rank 128 follows exactly from the verified paired-column Gram blocks; this agrees with the earlier reviewer contraction.

sources.locator: Count all half-edges in 4I0O and independently contract the four-leg Z/2 tensors; numerical corroboration recorded in independent_checks.gram.
